projects.title: Merger and Acquisition Copilot (BigQueryAI Hackathon)
projects.description: This project tackles the slow, costly, and high-risk manual review of unstructured legal documents during M&A due diligence. I introduce a warehouse-native paradigm, building an AI engine entirely within Google BigQuery to bring the AI securely to the data. Using a single SQL query, the solution leverages Object Tables to access raw PDFs, Gemini 2.5 Pro for multimodal analysis, and Vector Search for conceptual understanding. This transforms a chaotic data swamp into a structured, queryable risk report in seconds, delivering a powerful solution that combines the AI Architect, Semantic Detective, and Multimodal Pioneer tracks.

projects.title: Multimodal Drug Class Predictor
projects.description: Worked on an open source project to predict the Therapeutic class of a drug based on its Chemical Class and drug description using BERT architecture, achieving 99% accuracy.

projects.title: AlphaQuant
projects.description: Alpha Quant is an AI-powered financial analysis platform that lets users track real-time stock performance, receive the latest news and sentiment, and gain intelligent insights, as well as analyze different stock performances. With LSTM-based price predictions boasting 85%+ directional accuracy and smart sentiment analysis from a fine-tuned FinBERT model, Alpha Quant brings cutting-edge AI to personal investing. To further streamline the user experience, I implemented a RAG pipeline that allows users to upload their stock portfolios, after which their stock data is extracted and used to update their dashboards.

projects.title: Research Paper Implementation
projects.description: I implemented the HypKG research paper, which introduced the concept of contextualizing knowledge graphs (KGs) with patient-specific information from electronic health records (EHRs). By utilizing LLM-based entity-linking techniques (PromptLink) to connect biomedical knowledge with individual patient data, and employing hypergraph models to encode these contexts, I demonstrated how contextualizing knowledge graphs can significantly improve precision healthcare by considering unique patient conditions and features. This leads to better predictions and treatments. I published my thoughts and findings on the Medical Care Blog.

projects.title: GAN-Enhanced Skin Disease Diagnosis
projects.description: With the assistance of Generative Adversarial Networks, I generated approximately 3,000 synthetic images of dark skin to mitigate skin tone bias in the HAM1000 dataset, resulting in a 10% increase in the F1 score. Furthermore, I leveraged the Google Maps API to help users find the nearest clinic based on their location, thereby enhancing accessibility.
